I am Thoko, 23 years old, living here in Mzimba. This maize plot is not my own land — I rent it, so I must be careful how much I put into it. My husband and I received a fertilizer coupon from the government this year, so I will buy one bag of NPK for planting and one bag of urea for top-dressing — that is what the subsidy gives us. I intercrop with beans and pumpkins because we need food variety, and the beans help the soil a little. I cannot afford pesticide, and there is no river close enough to irrigate. My mother-in-law and my younger sister will help me with weeding when the rains come heavy.
